priors.claim: Generic leaderboards and tournament incentives constitute novel PFL mechanism
priors.reason: Prior causal/theoretical work predates campaign; Lemus and Marshall; Witkowski et al.

priors.claim: Game incentives can improve political forecast accuracy beyond strong baselines
priors.reason: No rights-cleared temporally frozen comparable panel
Exploratory literature search insufficient to establish absence

priors.claim: Weekly recorded Commons divisions in 2025 are unevenly exposed over time
priors.evidence: C02_RESULT.json, n322 unique, dispersion 5.1295 in 53 ISO weeks
priors.counter: Voting calendar/observed vote days account for much of variation; simple phenomenon known, not causal effect or N1

priors.claim: Opportunity concentration persists in a later calendar slice of same institution
priors.evidence: C03_RESULT.json Jan-Sept 2026 n195, dispersion 6.2378; 2025 seasonal n234, dispersion 5.962
priors.counter: Same data aggregator/issuer; 2025 earlier outcomes exposed; not independent prospective validation

priors.claim: Missing exposure is distinct from zero in PFL observatory
priors.counter: No real-person scoring or native full-suite run; logical QA only

priors.claim: One legislative issue can produce multiple recorded rollcalls affecting naive fantasy scoring opportunities
priors.evidence: C05_RESULT.json official House Clerk rows 200–299 in 2025, 51 issues, 62 rollcalls share repeated issue label
priors.counter: Each amendment/procedure is substantively distinct; issue capping is arbitrary; contiguous nonrandom segment; manual transcription corrected with errata

priors.claim: PFL-specific new scientific law established in this block
priors.evidence: No identification of incentive effects, no experiment with fantasy gamers, no independent prospective comparison, published prior art
